newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ govt hopes to exceed Tsy growth f'cst - Birch.
newsitem.headline: NZ govt hopes to exceed Tsy growth f'cst - Birch.

text.p: New Zealand finance minister Bill Birch said on Wednesday the government hoped to exceed Treasury's forecast of three to four percent growth per year for the rest of the decade.

"That's at the bottom of the range that we would hope to achieve, but that's about three times the growth rate that we did achieve through the '70s and '80s and it will indeed expand the NZ economy very rapidly," he told Radio New Zealand.
Birch said the government had a continuing intention of upgrading the economic framework that was working so well.

"That can be done without turning New Zealand on its head. We don't intend to turn New Zealand on its head, but we do intend to enhance and work on the framework of price stability, open economy, good labour market, enhancing the tax system and building the base and lowering the rates, and improving the performance of government and getting the debt down.
"All of those things are contributing to the growth that we're getting," he said.
Birch said the current framework gave investors, manufacturers, farmers and exporters the confidence to invest and expand the economy.
He said Treasury's forecasts were based on the best information available at the time.
